summary: Declares RFC 2731, on encoding Dublin Core metadata in HTML, obsolete, because further work on it moved to the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative. It is a short informational notice that retires the older document.

plainLanguage.summary: An old instruction sheet is stamped no longer used, because the people who made the idea now keep their own newer version.

questions: where did dublin core html encoding move
what is dublin core metadata in html
subtitle: RFC 2731 on putting Dublin Core metadata in HTML is retired because the Dublin Core initiative took over the work.

tldr.problem: RFC 2731 defined how to encode Dublin Core metadata in HTML, but newer Dublin Core Metadata Initiative specifications have overtaken it.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5791 obsoletes RFC 2731, noting that further development moved to the DCMI.
tldr.outcome: Implementers of RFC 2731 should read the DCMI's DC-HTML, which adds a new requirement for the head element's profile attribute.

today: RFC 5791 is an Informational memo that obsoletes RFC 2731. Development continues with the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative, and RFC 5791 has not been obsoleted itself.

sections.title: What Changed
sections.content:
RFC 2731 defined "Encoding Dublin Core Metadata in HTML". Over the last decade the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative (DCMI) published newer specifications, in particular "Expressing Dublin Core metadata using HTML/XHTML meta and link elements" (DC-HTML), which obsoleted that work.

This document obsoletes RFC 2731 because further development of the specification moved to the DCMI.
sections.plainLanguage: The group that invented the idea now writes its own up-to-date instructions, so the old sheet is retired.

sections.title: The Work Being Retired
sections.content:
RFC 2731 is titled "Encoding Dublin Core Metadata in HTML". The memo describes it only briefly: it was superseded by newer DCMI specifications published over the last decade, so the IETF no longer maintains a competing description.

The newer reference is the DCMI document "Expressing Dublin Core metadata using HTML/XHTML meta and link elements", dated August 2008.
sections.plainLanguage: Two groups had written instructions for the same job. Now only the inventors keep theirs.

sections.title: Note for Implementers
sections.content:
The memo adds one practical warning. Implementers of RFC 2731 should note that DC-HTML introduces a new requirement with respect to the use of the profile attribute of the head element.

The document is administrative only, and its security section says that there are no security relations related to it.
sections.plainLanguage: If you followed the old sheet, check the new one. It asks for one extra thing.

references.text: Kunze, J., "Encoding Dublin Core Metadata in HTML", RFC 2731, December 1999.
Johnston, P. and A. Powell, "Expressing Dublin Core metadata using HTML/XHTML meta and link elements", Dublin Core Metadata Initiative, August 2008.
